a: ‘Al-fajr’: the removal of the darkness of night by the light of morning.
‘Layalin’: plural of ‘laylah’ or ‘laylat’; it is from sunset to sunrise.
‘Ten nights’: the first ten of Dhu al-Hijjah.
‘Ash-shaf‘’: what makes another a pair; it is the opposite of the odd; and it is said that what is meant by ‘shaf‘’ is the Day of Sacrifice.
‘Al-witr’: the single among things; it is the opposite of the even; and it is said that what is meant is the Day of ‘Arafah.
Night: the time from sunset to sunrise.
An adverb that indicates, in most cases, future time.
‘Yasri’: originally ‘yasri’; ‘the night passes’: it goes on and departs.
A particle for asking about the content of a sentence; the question here is affirmative (taqrīrī).
A preposition conveying the meaning of figurative containment.
A demonstrative for the distant masculine singular; one person is addressed with it.
‘Dhi hijr’: one possessing intellect; intellect is called ‘hijr’ because it restrains its owner and prevents him from what his commanding soul calls him to.
‘Dhi hijr’: one possessing intellect; intellect is called ‘hijr’ because it restrains its owner and prevents him from what his commanding soul calls him to.
Lam: a particle for negating the imperfect (present) verb and turning it to the past.

‘Have you not seen’: an expression urging to look, to wonder, to take a lesson, and to reflect on the matter of those being spoken about; with this expression one addresses both whoever saw and whoever heard, and whoever did not see and did not hear.
A noun for questioning and clarifying the state.
‘Ad: the people of Hud, peace be upon him; an ancient tribe named after their father; their dwellings were at al-Ahqaf in the lands of Yemen.
It is said: the name of the town of ‘Ad, or the name of their ancestor after whom the tribe was named.
‘Possessor of pillars’: possessor of lofty buildings, or of tents having pillars.
A relative noun that applies to every feminine.
A particle for negating the imperfect (present) verb and turning it to the past.
‘Lam yukhlaq’: was not brought into being without a prior model; and Allah’s creation is from nothingness.
A preposition conveying the meaning of literal spatial containment.
Plural of ‘balad’; a balad is a bounded place in which groups settle.

An Arab people that perished before the appearance of Islam; named after one of the grandsons of Nuh, or so named because of the scarcity of water among them — it is said: ‘thamada al-ma’’, the water became scant; their prophet was Salih.
A relative noun for a group of males.
‘Jabu as-sakhr’: they cut the rock and carved their houses in it.
‘Al-wad’: the valley; it is Wadi al-Qura.
Fir‘awn: the title of the kings of Egypt in ancient history; what is meant is the well-known Pharaoh of Musa.
‘Possessor of stakes’: a description of Pharaoh; his stakes are the supports of his kingdom, such as soldiers and the like.
‘Possessor of stakes’: a description of Pharaoh; his stakes are the supports of his kingdom, such as soldiers and the like.
A relative noun for a group of males.
They acted tyrannically, despotically, and wronged.
A preposition conveying the meaning of literal spatial containment.
Plural of ‘balad’; a balad is a bounded place in which groups settle.
‘Fi’: a preposition conveying the meaning of literal spatial containment.
‘Your Lord poured upon them a scourge of punishment’: He brought down upon them a painful penalty.
‘Ala: a preposition conveying the meaning of literal superposition (being above).
‘A scourge of punishment’: severity of punishment.
A particle of emphasis and of the accusative, conveying emphasis of the content of the sentence.
‘Bil-mirsad’: lying in wait, that is, Allah gives respite to whoever disobeys Him for a little, then seizes him with the seizing of One Mighty and Powerful.
‘Amma’: a particle of detailing, emphasis, and condition, non-jussive.
The male and the female of the children of Adam.
An adverb that indicates, in most cases, future time.
Emphatic; its function is to compensate for an omitted verb or to emphasise the context in which it occurs.
He made easy and prepared for him the means of improving his state and of a pleasant life — either by giving or bringing about good, or by preventing or removing the disliked, or by both.
‘Amma’: a particle of detailing, emphasis, and condition, non-jussive.
An adverb that indicates, in most cases, future time.
Emphatic; its function is to compensate for an omitted verb or to emphasise the context in which it occurs.
‘He restricted his provision for him’: He narrowed his giving.
‘Ala: a preposition conveying the meaning of figurative superposition.
A particle that comes here for rebuttal by negating the answer.
A particle of commencement, non-conjunctive, conveying the meaning of transition or emphasis.
‘La tukrimun’: you do not treat kindly and do not do good.
One who lost his father before the age of maturity.
‘Wa la tahaddun’: and you do not urge one another, that is, some of you do not urge others.
Miskin: the poor one whom poverty has humbled.
‘You devour the inheritance’: you take it without right.
Originally ‘wurath’, the ‘waw’ replaced with ‘ta’: the wealth the deceased leaves behind, inherited from him.
‘Aklan lamma’: a greedy devouring, or gathering together the lawful and the unlawful.
‘Aklan lamma’: a greedy devouring, or gathering together the lawful and the unlawful.
Love of a thing: affection for it and the soul’s inclination toward it.
Mal (wealth): what is owned of goods, real estate, money, or animals.
Love of a thing: affection for it and the soul’s inclination toward it.
A particle negating the answer, coming for rebuke and deterrence.
An adverb that indicates, in most cases, future time.
‘The earth is crushed’: it is pounded and broken by earthquakes.
The well-known planet on whose surface we live, or a part of it.
‘Dakkan dakkan’: crushing after crushing until it became dust.

‘Al-malak’: the kind of the angels; the angels: a kind of Allah the Exalted’s creation; they have subtle bodies of light and take whatever forms they wish; they do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded.
‘Saffan saffan’: arranged in rows upon rows.
‘Saffan saffan’: arranged in rows upon rows.
‘Hell is brought’: it is brought forth.
Jahannam: the fire with which punishment is given in the Hereafter.

‘Yatadhakkar’: he calls to mind — from remembrance, the opposite of forgetting; that is, he remembers his negligence in the world and its effect at that moment, and this drives him to feel admonition and repentance at a time when neither admonition nor repentance benefits.
The male and the female of the children of Adam.
‘Anna’: an adverb of place used for asking, in the meaning of ‘kayfa’ (how) or ‘min ayna’ (from where).

Lam: a preposition conveying specification; the meaning of ‘how will he have the remembrance’: how will admonition and repentance benefit him, when he neglected them in the world and their time has passed.
‘Ya’: a particle of drawing attention combined with wishing; ‘layta’: a particle resembling a verb, conveying a wish, usually connected with the impossible.
‘I had sent forth for my life’: I had done (deeds) for my Hereafter.
For my life in the Hereafter after the resurrection.
‘La yu‘adhdhibu’: does not penalise or punish severely.
A noun for everyone who is fit to be addressed.
‘Bind his binding’: tie him with chains and shackles.
Wathaq: a binding, or chains, shackles, and the like with which one is tied.
A noun for everyone who is fit to be addressed.
‘Ya’ is for calling; ‘ayyatuha’ is a link for calling females that have ‘al’.
‘The tranquil soul’: the content, calm soul, at rest in faith and affirming the reward and the resurrection.
‘The tranquil soul’: the content, calm soul, at rest in faith and affirming the reward and the resurrection.
‘Return to your Lord’: go back to His good pleasure.
A preposition indicating the end of the extent.
To your God who is worshipped.
Possessing a soul content with what it has been given.
‘Enter among My servants’: enter among the righteous servants of Allah, those who worship and obey Me.
A preposition conveying accompaniment in the meaning of ‘ma‘a’ (with).
Those who worship and obey Me.
Entering a place: passing through its entrance and reaching its interior.
‘Jannah’ in this world is a garden with trees, rivers, and fruits; ‘jannah’ in the Hereafter is the abode of lasting bliss after death.
